subject: Partner Enablement: Tiered Captures & Registration Window

Date: Sun, 28 Apr 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partner Enablement: Tiered Captures & Registration Window

Hi Ava —

Great speaking earlier. As discussed, CloudScale's customers are a good fit for a lightweight reseller arrangement where you (CloudScale) can register leads and earn a referral/commission on closed ARR. Two items I wanted to lock down to move to legal/ops:

1) Tiered capture window: we typically offer a 90-day lead protection window from first registration, with a 12-month attribution period if the lead is registered and engaged. For larger partner-led deals we can extend to 180 days. Can you confirm whether CloudScale needs standard or extended protection?

2) Commission tiers: our proposal (high-level) is 8% on first-year ARR for self-sourced leads under $200k, 12% for $200k–$1M, and a 15% flat on >$1M deals with an ops-stair for multi-year contracts. We can structure payout as one-time on signed order or split over first two quarters.

I've copied Marissa (partnerships) and Lauren (channel ops) to help draft a clean registration process and an onboarding MOP. If you agree in principle, I can send a one-page registration template and a short MOP spreadsheet for CloudScale to confirm.

Next step: are you ok with the 90-day window vs needing 180? If the latter, let us know the expected deal cadence so we can justify the exception.

Thanks —
Ben

Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap.

Quick answers: CloudScale prefers a 180-day registration window for partner-sourced leads. Our sales cycle for the core verticals you and I discussed (finserv + healthcare tooling partners) often stretches beyond 90 days; 180 would be helpful to protect our investment in lead development.

On commissions, the tier bands look reasonable. Two small asks:
- For deals between $200k–$1M can we have a two-step payout (50% on signature, 50% 90 days post-go-live)?
- Can you carve out a small marketing co-fund for joint events (we typically ask for USD 5k co-op per quarter during ramp)?

If you send the registration template and the MOP spreadsheet, I will route to my ops and procurement for an early look.

Best,

Hi all — looping in a couple operational clarifications (copied inline):

> Default window set to 180 days for CloudScale (we can annotate exceptions for enterprise accounts)

We can set 180 days for registration. Two operational constraints:
- Lead registration must include a minimum qualifying data set (company, contact, initial value estimate, channel rep, lead source, and first outreach date). If that dataset isn't present we mark the registration as provisional and give partners 14 days to complete.
- Attribution after registration: if Redwood responds to the lead with product demo within 30 days, internal routing rules kick in and sales-assist may convert the lead to Redwood-sourced. We surface that in the MOP but want alignment that CloudScale will not list the same lead twice.

On payout schedule: 50/50 split on the $200k–$1M band is reasonable. For >$1M deals we prefer milestone-triggered payments (50% on signature, 25% at production acceptance, 25% at 6 months).

Marissa — are there any thresholds where we need executive approval for an extended co-op (>$5k/quarter)?

—Lauren

Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — procurement wants formal pricing and a DocuSign-ready agreement. They also requested an explicit naming convention for registrations so they can ingest records into our PRM. Can you: 

1) Provide the one-page registration PDF with a suggested registration ID format (e.g., CS-REG-YYYYMMDD-XXXX)
2) Share a DocuSign link (or sandbox) with the simplified SOW + partner exhibit that includes the 180-day window, 50/50 split for the mid band, and the co-op line at $5k/quarter

Marissa — appreciate if you can confirm whether a >$5k/quarter co-op needs executive approval or if you can sign. If you need an approval path, I can pause and route procurement accordingly.

If you prefer, Ben and I can hop on a short call Monday to finalize the fields and get the DocuSign over.

Best,
Ava Turner
